newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh PM praises India for water pact.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh PM praises India for water pact.

text.p: Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Friday praised Indian leaders for their role in striking a long-term pact on sharing Ganges River water, saying it was a milestone in relations between the countries.
"I want to thank Indian leaders for their cooperation in reaching the treaty. This will strengthen our relations with India," Hasina told a news conference.
Hasina and Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda signed the 30-year, water-sharing agreement in New Delhi on Thursday.
"It was a long-standing water dispute. And this is the first treaty and a historic event," she said.
Hasina, whose party won a general election last June, said her government had kept its promise.
"It was our pledge to the nation that Bangladesh must gain its rightful share of the Ganges water. It has been fulfilled."
Thousands of people greeted the prime minister when she returned home on Thursday night after signing the landmark agreement in India.
The water dispute has festered since 1974 when India built the Farakka Barrage to curb the flow of the Ganges, which irrigates much of northern India before flowing into Bangladesh.

In 1977, the two nations signed an agreement allowing Bangladesh a guaranteed minimum of 34,000 cubic feet of water per second between October and June every year. But the guarantee was dropped in a new six-year accord signed in 1982.
Under the new treaty, the two countries will evenly share scarce water in the dry season from March to May. The treaty assures them both minimum amounts of water in other months.
